chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who broke his fast for one day from the month of Ramadan deliberately, so he (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I am destroyed, O Messenger of Allah.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'The Fire, O Messenger of Allah.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what is the matter with you?' He said, 'I had intercourse with my wife.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Give in charity and seek forgiveness.' The man said, 'By the One who magnified your right, I have not left in the house anything, neither little nor much.'

He (the narrator) said: 'Then a man from the people entered with a sack of dates containing twenty sa', which is ten sa' by our sa'. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Take these dates and give in charity with them.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, upon whom shall I give in charity with them, and I have informed you that there is neither little nor much in my house?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So take it and feed it to your dependents and seek forgiveness of Allah.'
He (the narrator) said: 'So when we came out, our companions said, 'He began with emancipation.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Emancipate, or fast, or give in charity.'

key_terms.صَاع: A unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking the fast in Ramadan through intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the hierarchy of *kaffarah* (expiation) for deliberate fasting violation, specifically highlighting the flexibility in the final stage of feeding the poor. While the standard sequence mandates freeing a slave, then fasting, then feeding sixty poor, the Prophet’s provision of dates to the impoverished man demonstrates the scholarly principle that feeding one's own dependents can suffice if the individual lacks the means to feed others directly, emphasizing mercy over rigid formalism. This narrative is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the practical application of financial capacity (*istita'ah*) in expiation rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who breaks a Fast for a day from the Month of Ramazan, deliberately. So he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘I am destroyed, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is the matter?’ So he said, ‘The Fire, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And what is the matter?’ He said, ‘I fell upon my wife’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give in charity and seek Forgiveness’. So the man said, ‘By the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who Magnified your<sup>saww</sup> rights, nothing is left in the house, neither less nor more’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man from the people came over with a sack of dates in which were twenty Sa’as (a unit of measurement), which happens to be ten Sa’as by (the measurement) of our Sa’as’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Take these dates and give in charity with it’. So he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Whom shall I give it in charity with it, and I have informed you<sup>saww</sup> that there is neither in my house anything less nor more?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So take it and feed it to your dependents and seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we came out, our companions said, ‘It has to be begun with the emancipation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Emancipate, or Fast, or charity’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who purposely destroys one day of the fast of the month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said,

‘Once a man came to the Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, “O Messenger of Allah!” He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, “What is the matter with you?” He replied, “I fell on my wife.” He (the Messenger of Allah) said, “Give charity and repent.” He (the man) said, “I swear by the One who has made your right great, there is nothing in my house small and very little or large and a great deal.”

He (the Imam) said that a man then came with a massive bushel of dates which was twenty Sa‘, each of which was equal to ten of our Sa‘. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said to him (the man), “Take this and give it as charity.” He (the man) said, “O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I give this charity when I have told you that in my house there is nothing little or a great deal.” He (the Messenger of Allah) said, “Take it and feed your family and ask Allah for forgiveness.’”
He (the narrator) has said that when we came out (of the meeting) our people told us that expiation is to set free a slave saying, ‘Set free a slave, fast or give charity.’”
